newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan to spend 215 million sterling to make 3rd car in UK.
newsitem.headline: Nissan to spend 215 million sterling to make 3rd car in UK.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would invest 215 million pounds to start making a third car model in Britain.

Nissan will create 800 new jobs by the year 2000 to add the third model to the production line at Nissan Motor Mfg (UK) Ltd (NMUK) in Sunderland, Northeast England. The investment will be used to make production equipment such as moulds for the car.
A spokesman for Nissan, Japan's second-biggest carmaker, said it will produce Pulsar models at the plant from the year 2000. The cars have 1400 to 1600 cc engines.
The British unit had a total of 4,000 employees as of the end of 1995, the spokesman said.
Production of the Pulsar, called the Almera in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, is also expected to create 4,000 jobs in European car parts suppliers providing components to NMUK.
NMUK produced 232,000 cars in calendar 1996, including 137,000 Micras and 95,000 Primeras. NMUK will boost its production to about 266,000 cars in 1997, the Nissan spokesman said.
